get.description: Top values on the articles matching the search; each count is matching articles.
The articles and stories behind one graph edge, under the same filters as the graph.

CompareClusterResponse.title: CompareClusterResponse
CompareClusterResponse.description: Subject articles in the window that the story holds.

CompareOverlap.title: CompareOverlap
CompareOverlap.description:
Articles are distinct articles; stories are clusters holding an article of the subject; a
story is `both` when it holds one of each. `sources` (distinct feeds) is null for sources.

CompareRelated.title: CompareRelated
CompareRelated.description:
Top items over the union of both article sets, ranked by `a_articles + b_articles`. Zero
means absent from that side. The compared subjects are left out.

CompareSide.title: CompareSide
CompareSide.description:
Counts are over the subject's articles dated in the window. `sources` is null when the
subject is itself a source.

EventClusterResponse.title: EventClusterResponse
EventClusterResponse.description: A member cluster with the stored reason it joined the event.

EventSummary.title: EventSummary
EventSummary.description:
`cluster_count`, `article_count` and `source_count` are aggregated when asked, never stored.

An event has no title of its own: `headline` is the title of the representative article of its
largest member cluster (ties: earliest first publication, then cluster id).

EventTimelineDay.title: EventTimelineDay
EventTimelineDay.description: One UTC day of the event's articles; `evidence` is the day's earliest articles (up to 3).

GeoArticlePage.title: GeoArticlePage
GeoArticlePage.description:
`skipped_stale`: hits on this page whose article PostgreSQL no longer holds (the index lags a
merge or deletion); they are skipped rather than replaced, and paging continues past them.

GeoCountriesResponse.title: GeoCountriesResponse
GeoCountriesResponse.description:
`scope=recent` counts are exact, from PostgreSQL over the last `days`. `scope=investigation`
counts come from Elasticsearch over the shared search criteria, bounded only by their own
`after`/`before` (`window_start`/`window_end`, either may be open): articles and coverage are
exact document counts, stories and sources cardinality estimates, as the flags say.

GeoCountry.title: GeoCountry
GeoCountry.description:
Counts for one country in one role. An article with several countries counts once in each.
`articles` and `stories` are null for the `event` role, `events` is null for every other role,
and `sources` (distinct feeds) is only set for the `source` role.

GeoCoverage.title: GeoCoverage
GeoCoverage.description:
The base of every count: `window_total` items (articles, or events) in the window, of which
`located` have a country in this role.

InvestigationState.title: InvestigationState
InvestigationState.description: Complete search investigation, using the /search query parameter names.

MonitorChanges.title: MonitorChanges
MonitorChanges.description: What `(window_start, window_end]` brought that the monitor had not matched before.

Overlap.title: Overlap
Overlap.description: Two sets, A and B. `jaccard` is `both / union` and null when the union is empty.

SourceClusterResponse.title: SourceClusterResponse
SourceClusterResponse.description: `first`/`minutes_behind` are null for a story only this source published.

SourceExtraction.title: SourceExtraction
SourceExtraction.description:
Every count is out of `articles`. `not_extracted` is what is left: no content, no failed or
active job (an RSS-only feed never requests extraction).

SourceHealth.title: SourceHealth
SourceHealth.description: Derived from the feed row and its fetch history; there is no stored health score.

SourcePublishing.title: SourcePublishing
SourcePublishing.description: `with_published_at` is out of `articles`: the rest use the discovery time as their date.

SourceTiming.title: SourceTiming
SourceTiming.description:
Over stories in the window that this source and at least one other source published.

`first` counts stories where this source's article is the earliest (ties: lowest article id; an
article that several feeds carry counts for each of them). The two minute values describe the
remaining stories: how far behind the earliest article this source's own article was.
